evidenceBoundary: Deterministic local-Git fixtures and static command-policy tests only. No remote, GitHub, cloud inference, or production deployment was invoked.
problemsRecovered: A forced checkpoint restore replayed checkpoint files but could leave a newly created non-ignored untracked file in the workspace while reporting success.

The command classifier described every git branch form as read-only even though branch forms can create, move, or delete refs; git diff external-helper and output-file forms could also be treated as ordinary inspection.
Context-pack assembly trusted the current repository index until a caller explicitly refreshed it, so a Git checkout performed outside the runtime could select symbols from the prior revision.

change.checkpointRestore: force:true now runs git clean -fd -- before restoring the durable checkpoint snapshot. The existing divergence guard still blocks non-forced restores before any mutation. The checkpoint only captures non-ignored untracked content, matching git stash -u.
change.commandPolicy: git branch/worktree/workspace-ref mutation forms are project-modifying rather than read-only; git diff --ext-diff, --textconv, and --output are critical execution boundaries.
change.revisionFreshness: IndexStatus exposes the revision recorded by the last index refresh. buildContextPack compares it with live HEAD and refreshes before retrieval on a mismatch, preserving content-addressed reuse for unchanged files.

proven: A force-authorized restore removes a file created after the checkpoint and reproduces the captured staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked state from a real temporary Git repository.
A non-forced restore still fails closed on a divergent dirty workspace before any restore operation.
Mutating Git branch/worktree/ref commands do not receive a read-only classification, and configured diff-helper or output-file execution is denied to autonomous runs as critical.

A branch checkout outside the runtime triggers a context-index refresh before context retrieval; the resulting pack contains the new-branch symbol, excludes the old-branch symbol, and reports the new branch.
The renderer-to-main Git bridge remains limited to validated read-only workspace/identity queries, and linked worktrees are identified and isolated by actual Git directory topology.
notProven: Remote operations, GitHub workflows, push/pull/fetch behavior, credentials, or hosting integrations.

All possible external dirty-working-tree mutations that leave HEAD unchanged; in-run successful mutations already refresh, and delivered file chunks are hash-checked, but a no-HEAD external change is not a general filesystem watcher.
Live-model Git command selection, autonomous engineering completion, or packaged desktop behavior after a fresh build.
requiredNextEvidence: For live proof, run paired free-route engineering tasks that include an approved branch switch or checkpoint restore, then retain route, Git-status, context-generation, verifier, and completion-gate receipts. Keep remote operations in an explicitly authorized disposable repository.
